questions.stem: The father of modern genetics is:
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel (1822-84), an Augustinian friar, worked out the laws of inheritance by cross-breeding pea plants — published in 1866 but ignored till rediscovered around 1900. Charles Darwin proposed natural selection; Louis Pasteur pioneered microbiology and vaccines; Watson, Crick (with Franklin and Wilkins) proposed the double helix of DNA in 1953.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: A normal human body cell contains how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: 46 chromosomes arranged as 23 pairs — 22 pairs of autosomes plus 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males). Gametes (sperm and ovum) are haploid with just 23 chromosomes each. Chimpanzees and gorillas have 48; mosquitoes have 6; bread wheat has 42.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The genetic material in most living organisms is:
questions.explanation: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is the hereditary material in almost all organisms, from bacteria to humans. It is a double-stranded helix of four bases — A, T, G, C — held together by complementary pairing (A-T, G-C). A small number of viruses (HIV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2) use RNA as their genetic material instead.

questions.stem: Colour blindness in humans is an example of:
questions.explanation: Colour-blindness genes lie on the X chromosome and are recessive. Males (XY) need only one faulty allele to be colour-blind; females (XX) need both X chromosomes to carry it. This is why colour-blindness is far more common in men. Haemophilia and Duchenne muscular dystrophy have the same pattern. Y-linked traits pass only father-to-son.

questions.stem: In a cross between a pure tall pea plant (TT) and a pure dwarf pea plant (tt), the F1 generation will all be:
questions.explanation: TT × tt → all offspring are Tt (heterozygous). Because T (tall) is dominant over t (dwarf), the F1 plants all look tall but carry the dwarf allele. When F1 plants self-cross (Tt × Tt), the F2 generation shows a 3:1 phenotypic ratio (tall : dwarf) — Mendel's Law of Segregation.

questions.stem: The double-helix structure of DNA was proposed in 1953 by:
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick, working at Cambridge, published the double-helix model in Nature on 25 April 1953. They drew crucially on Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 X-ray diffraction image and Maurice Wilkins's data; Watson, Crick and Wilkins shared the 1962 Nobel (Franklin had died in 1958 and the Nobel is not awarded posthumously).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: A segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein or function is called a:
questions.explanation: A gene is a functional unit of heredity — a stretch of DNA carrying instructions for a specific protein (or RNA). Humans have around 20,000 protein-coding genes. A chromosome is a packaged bundle of DNA containing many genes; ribosomes are cellular factories that translate mRNA into protein; a nucleotide is a single A/T/G/C building block of DNA.
